tagline.en: The Qing post road down the western plain, made a gravel motor road by the Japanese and joined up only when the Xiluo bridge opened in 1953
tagline.zh: 沿西部平原南下的清代官道，日治时期修成碎石车道，直到 1953 年西螺大桥通车才真正贯通

start.en: Zhongxiao West Road at Zhongshan South Road, outside the Executive Yuan in Taipei — the zero point of Taiwan's highways
start.zh: 台北市中正区忠孝西路与中山南路口，行政院大门前——台湾公路原点

end.en: Fenggang, Fangshan, Pingtung, where it meets Provincial Highways 9 and 26
end.zh: 屏东县枋山乡枫港，与台 9 线、台 26 线相接

en: Provincial Highway 1 is the old main street of western Taiwan. It leaves Taipei over the Zhongxiao bridge and runs south through every western city and county except Keelung and Nantou — Taoyuan, Hsinchu, Miaoli, Taichung, Changhua, Yunlin, Chiayi, Tainan, Kaohsiung — to Fenggang near the island's southern tip. With Highway 9 on the east it makes the round-the-island road, and since the Suhua and South Link improvements shortened Highway 9 it is again the longest provincial highway.

Before the freeways it was the island's north–south road, and it still links most of the big western towns, though it now usually skirts their centres on four-lane bypasses. Many of the old in-town alignments survive under branch numbers, and local usage has not kept up: between Taipei and Taoyuan the old road, now Highway 1A, is still called the 'first provincial road', while the newer main line, Xinbei Boulevard, is called the 'second'.

It is a lowland road. Its highest point is only 181 m, at the 43.5 km mark in Puxin, Yangmei. On the Pingtung coast road at Jiadong one straight stretch is a wartime runway, the only one on a provincial highway.
zh: 台 1 线是台湾西部的老“大街”。它自台北经忠孝桥出城，一路南下，经过除基隆市与南投县以外的所有西部县市——桃园、新竹、苗栗、台中、彰化、云林、嘉义、台南、高雄——抵达岛屿南端附近的枫港。它与东部的台 9 线大致构成环岛公路；苏花改与南回改使台 9 线缩短后，台 1 线再度成为里程最长的省道。
高速公路出现之前，它就是全岛的南北干道，至今仍串连大多数西部大城镇，只是如今多半改走四线道的外环道绕过市中心。许多旧的市区路段以支线编号保留下来，民间称呼却没有跟着改：台北至桃园之间，旧线（今台 1 甲线）仍被叫作“一省道”，较新的正线新北大道反而被叫作“二省道”。
这是一条平原公路，最高点仅海拔 181 米，位于桃园市杨梅区埔心里 43.5 公里处。屏鹅公路佳冬段有一段笔直路面兼作战备跑道，是唯一设在省道上的战备道。

en: The line goes back to the Qing post road, laid out from 1684 between the prefectural city at Tainan and the county seats. The historian who wrote a history of Highway 1, 省道台一線的故事, argues that it wound about because it was routed past the lowland indigenous villages whose people were made to carry mail, drive carts and repair the road. The Qing never made it much more than a track: it shifted with every storm, and after repeated revolts the authorities deliberately left rivers unbridged so that rebels could not use it.

Soon after 1895 the Japanese set about widening the old paths into a road that army lorries could use, from Keelung to Pingtung. At first it had no bridges and only a gravel surface. In 1916 the 461.7 km gravel road was named the Zongguan Road (North–South Road), given a design standard and made a 'designated road', improved and maintained from national or local funds.

Bridging the rivers took decades. By the end of 1935 only the Zhuoshui and the Lower Danshui (now Gaoping) still had no road crossing for motor vehicles. Towns on both banks of the Zhuoshui petitioned for a bridge from 1934; the colonial government planned one at 3.2 million yen over five years, and the piers were built from 1938 to 1941 before the war took the steel. After 1945 the work was taken up again with American aid, and the Xiluo bridge, 1,939 m long, opened on 28 January 1953, completing the through road that had been laid out under the Japanese.

The road had been badly damaged by American bombing in the war. Before 1952 only Keelung–Taoyuan and Tainan–Kaohsiung had concrete or asphalt; from 1952 to 1956 the stretch from Taoyuan to Tainan was given a penetration asphalt surface. When the provincial highways were numbered in 1965 Highway 1 ran 501.098 km from the Executive Yuan to the Eluanbi lighthouse. In 1978 it was cut back to end at Fenggang, and in 1994 it was moved onto bypasses around Sanchong, Xinzhuang, Guishan, Taoyuan, Zhongli and Tainan, with the old Taipei–Taoyuan road renumbered Highway 1A.
zh: 这条路线可以追溯到清代官道：1684 年起，以台湾府城（今台南）为中心，串连南北各县治。历史研究者黄智伟认为，官道之所以弯弯曲曲，是因为它要经过各个平埔番社，而递送公文、驾驶牛车、修路等劳役都由番民负担。清廷始终没有把它修成像样的道路：路线常因风雨偏移改道，而且历经多次反清事件后，官府为了不让叛军沿官道逃窜，刻意不架桥、不修路。
1895 年日本领台后不久，为军事交通之便，开始把清代留下的羊肠小径拓宽成军用卡车也能通行的道路，自基隆通到屏东。起初不建桥，只铺砂石。1916 年，这条全长 461.7 公里的碎石路定名为“纵贯道”，订立道路标准，列为以国库或地方经费改善养护的“指定道路”。
跨河花了几十年。到 1935 年底，纵贯道路只剩浊水溪与下淡水溪（今高屏溪）两处汽车无法通行。浊水溪两岸街庄自 1934 年起陆续陈情建桥；总督府拟以 320 万圆、分五个年度兴建，1938 至 1941 年完成桥墩后，钢材因战争挪作他用而停工。1945 年后在美援协助下续建，全长 1,939 米的西螺大桥于 1953 年 1 月 28 日通车，日治时期定线的纵贯道路至此全线贯通。
二战期间美军轰炸使道路残破不堪。1952 年以前，只有基隆至桃园、台南至高雄两段铺有混凝土或沥青路面；1952 至 1956 年，桃园至台南之间铺设灌入式沥青路面。1965 年编定省道编号时，台 1 线自行政院至鹅銮鼻灯塔，全长 501.098 公里；1978 年改以枫港为终点；1994 年改经三重、新庄、龟山、桃园、中坜、台南等地的外环道，原台北至桃园路段改编为台 1 甲线。

en: The Xiluo bridge is a Warren through-truss of 31 spans on 30 piers, 7.32 m wide. The Japanese sank its piers as oval caissons 20.3 m deep; the steel trusses were made by US Steel and erected in 1952 from both ends at once by the Resources Commission's engineering office and Taiwan Machinery, with Filipino workers. When finished it was described as the second-largest bridge in the world after the Golden Gate and the longest in the Far East. It also carried a sugar-railway track until 1979.

Widening to four lanes began after 1970, as traffic on parts of the road built up, and was finished in 1997. In 1994 the new Xizhou bridge took Highway 1 across the Zhuoshui, and the Xiluo bridge was handed down to County Road 145; its scoured Japanese piers 10 to 25 were rebuilt from 2004 to 2011, in the original style, without closing the bridge.
zh: 西螺大桥为下承式华伦式钢桁架桥，31 孔、桥墩 30 座，桥宽 7.32 米。日治时期以深 20.3 米的椭圆形沉箱为桥墩基础；钢桁梁由美国钢铁公司制造，1952 年由资源委员会机械工程处与台湾机械公司配合菲律宾技工，自南北两端同时向中间架设。完工时号称仅次于美国金门大桥的世界第二大桥、“远东第一大桥”。桥上还并设台糖铁路，直到 1979 年拆除。
1970 年以后，部分路段交通日渐壅塞，开始拓宽为四线道，至 1997 年完工。1994 年新建的溪州大桥接手台 1 线跨越浊水溪，西螺大桥改隶县道 145 号；其日治时期的第 10 至 25 号桥墩因河床冲刷而裸露，2004 至 2011 年依原样式重建，施工期间未中断桥上交通。

en: No cost has been published for the road as a whole, which was built up over three centuries. The figures that exist are for its key bridge. The Japanese planned the Zhuoshui bridge at 3.2 million yen and spent 494,000 yen on the piers and abutments. To finish it, the US State Department approved US$1.3 million in 1951 to buy the steel, the provincial government put in its own budget, and the trusses and deck cost NT$73.7 million.
The bridge was also where Taiwan began charging tolls on bridges: from 29 January 1953, the day after it opened, cars and motorcycles paid to cross.
zh: 这条路历经三个世纪逐步修成，没有整条路线的造价，现有数字都属于它最关键的那座桥。日治时期浊水溪桥预算 320 万圆，桥台与桥墩实际花费 49 万 4 千日圆。战后续建时，美国国务院于 1951 年核准 130 万美元购买钢材，另由省府编列预算，桁梁与桥面工程费为新台币 7,370 万元。
这座桥也开了台湾桥梁收费的先例：通车次日、1953 年 1 月 29 日起，向通行的汽机车征收通行费。

en: Limits are 40 to 70 km/h. Kilometre posts count south from Taipei. Expect a town road for much of the way, with signals, scooters and frontage shops; for through travel the freeways have long since taken over, and Highway 1 is used in pieces. The Xiluo bridge, on County Road 145 a short way downstream of Highway 1's Xizhou bridge, is open to light traffic and is a listed historic building, but it is closed for strengthening from December 2025 to January 2027.
zh: 速限为每小时 40 至 70 公里；里程桩自台北起向南递增。沿途大部分路段是市镇道路，有号志、机车与沿街店面；长途旅行早已交给高速公路，台 1 线多半是分段使用。西螺大桥位于台 1 线溪州大桥下游不远处，属县道 145 号，开放小型车通行，并已登录为历史建筑，但 2025 年 12 月至 2027 年 1 月封桥进行补强。

why.en: Highway 1 grew out of the Qing post road and was widened, paved and bridged piecemeal by the Japanese and the provincial highway bureau from the 1890s to 1997; no cost for the whole road has been published. The Xiluo bridge, its key link, is given below.
why.zh: 台 1 线源自清代官道，自 1890 年代至 1997 年由日治当局与省公路局陆续拓宽、铺面、架桥，没有公布过整条路线的造价。其关键路段西螺大桥列于下方。

value.en: 494,000 yen for the piers and abutments (1938–1941); NT$73.7 million for the trusses and deck (1952)
value.zh: 桥台与桥墩 49 万 4 千日圆（1938—1941 年）；桁梁与桥面新台币 7,370 万元（1952 年）

figures.source: Taiwan Nichi Nichi Shimpo, 1 March 1939, and other contemporary reports, as cited in Chinese Wikipedia, 西螺大橋

value.en: Under the Japanese, a 'designated road' improved and maintained from national or local funds. After 1945 repair and the Xiluo bridge were paid for with American aid — US$1.3 million for the bridge steel — and the provincial budget.
value.zh: 日治时期列为以国库或地方经费改善养护的“指定道路”；战后修复及西螺大桥由美援（桥梁钢材 130 万美元）与省府预算支应。

figures.source: Rhythms Monthly, 台灣脈動：省道的築夢與築路 (2008), as cited in Chinese Wikipedia, 台1線; Chinese Wikipedia, 西螺大橋

value.en: 461.7 km of gravel road, Keelung to Pingtung, when named the Zongguan Road
value.zh: 定名“纵贯道”时为 461.7 公里碎石路，自基隆至屏东

figures.source: Rhythms Monthly, 台灣脈動：省道的築夢與築路 (2008), as cited in Chinese Wikipedia, 台1線

value.en: 501.098 km in 1965, Executive Yuan to Eluanbi lighthouse; 456.717 km after the 1978 cut-back to Fenggang
value.zh: 1965 年 501.098 公里（行政院至鹅銮鼻灯塔）；1978 年改以枫港为终点后为 456.717 公里

timeline.en: The Qing lay out a post road north and south from the prefectural city at Tainan.
timeline.zh: 清廷以台湾府城为中心，建立南北官道。

timeline.en: The Japanese name the 461.7 km gravel road from Keelung to Pingtung the Zongguan Road.
timeline.zh: 日人将基隆至屏东 461.7 公里碎石路定名为“纵贯道”。

timeline.en: By the year's end only the Zhuoshui and Lower Danshui rivers lack a motor-road crossing.
timeline.zh: 年底时，纵贯道路只剩浊水溪与下淡水溪无法通行汽车。

timeline.en: The Zhuoshui bridge piers are finished; work stops for want of steel.
timeline.zh: 浊水溪桥桥墩完工，其后因缺乏钢材停工。

timeline.en: The Xiluo bridge opens on 28 January, completing the through road; tolls begin the next day.
timeline.zh: 1 月 28 日西螺大桥通车，纵贯道路全线贯通；次日开始收费。

timeline.en: Penetration asphalt surfacing from Taoyuan to Tainan, begun in 1952, is completed.
timeline.zh: 1952 年开始的桃园至台南灌入式沥青路面工程完成。

timeline.en: Numbered Highway 1, 501.098 km from the Executive Yuan to Eluanbi.
timeline.zh: 编为台 1 线，自行政院至鹅銮鼻，长 501.098 公里。

timeline.en: The southern end is moved back to Fenggang.
Moved onto town bypasses; the old Taipei–Taoyuan road becomes 1A; the Xizhou bridge replaces the Xiluo bridge.
timeline.zh: 改经各市区外环道，原台北至桃园旧线改为台 1 甲线；溪州大桥取代西螺大桥。

timeline.en: Widening to four lanes, begun after 1970, is finished.
timeline.zh: 1970 年后展开的四线道拓宽工程完工。
